acceptance.continuation_threshold: the mean surprise of the corpus's own held-out continuations under the event model fitted on the training split and frozen: 235 phrases, 1.6079 nats per note event
acceptance.note: This stage is accepted on what it does with a phrase it heard: the instrument gates, the two imitation gates under voiced listening, the continuation measure, the imitation control margins, latency, the block cap and the renderer faults. Composition under a request, the theme that returns and the live revision are measured every run and reported open: they carry their values and thresholds in the receipt under 'open' and they do not enter acceptance.passed. Composition is open because the judge here is the reference judge and the packet asks for a listener panel; the theme is open because a step read back out of the declared store names the note that was played in 0.05 of the blocks; revision is the compose path and moves with it.

assumptions: The world head is a records cortex whose reading is the sensory and efference neurons: the 68 hearing features of the mix and of each voice, one flag saying whether this body may play or another player is sounding, and the 541 motor neurons of the executed gesture. The goal port and the reads of the stores are not in that reading, because what a gesture does to the sound does not depend on what is wanted or on which phrase is running, and S05a measured what a goal inside the reading costs (NOTES.md sections 10 to 12). ReadingConfig puts either of them back and the pilot measures the difference.

The consequence head predicts the change of every hearing field from the block the decision was taken in, not the next hearing. Predicting zero is then persistence, which is what carried the overall prediction gate in S05a round two, and only the change is left to learn.

One voice is revised per decision and the other two hold. A gesture is held for three blocks while playing and six in free play, because the ear hears 120 ms and a search of one block rejects every change for the mixture it must pass through (S05a section 9).

The candidate set is a coarse pitch grid of every third semitone with a refinement of two semitones around the winner, the waveforms of the note the voice holds, the rest and the gesture already playing. Every so often the revision falls on the shared fields instead, where the cutoff and the volume are the candidates.

The preference store is a records cortex keyed by the phrase digest and the goal port, with the two as declared pathways and the requested attribute's known flag selecting the cells. One write per judged phrase at rate one. The planner reads it when it composes.
The reference judge is supplied and is not a listener panel. The packet's preference gate needs real listeners; what this run reports under a judge is a stand-in and is declared as one.
Checkpoints are written between episodes, where no decision awaits its outcome, so a restored life continues exactly.

Free play draws its gestures from what the ear can hear. The environment calls a renderer failure when a voice its envelope model says should sound makes none for four blocks; the model reads the volume and the sustain as switches and the ear reads level, calling anything under -50 dBFS silence. Measured on the chip, three regions of the codec fall between them: the two slowest attack bins, which take 800 ms and 8 s to reach their sustain and are still under the threshold four blocks after the gate rises; a gated voice at sustain 9 under volume 2, which reads -67 dBFS; and the lowest sustains under a volume that is not full. Eleven renderer failures in eleven free-play episodes of the first pilot came from them, and two in four episodes after the first repair. Free play draws the attack from the six faster bins, the volume from 11 upward and a nonzero sustain from 2 upward.

A new note is played as a release and then the note. The chip moves the pitch of a gated voice without starting the note again, so a planner that only ever raises gates plays one sliding note per voice: the first pilot's compositions hold three gates for two hundred blocks and the ear measures almost no note in them.

The mix is transcribed at 128 geometric bands, 19.3 to an octave, which the listener computes itself from World.audio; the supplied 68 features and the three monitors are untouched. Measured on six held-out phrases and 906 sounding blocks, a harmonic comb reads the exact pitch in 0.529 of them at 64 bands, 0.619 at 128 and 0.590 at 192 when the number of voices sounding is given, so 128 is adopted and 192 buys nothing.

The comb peels one fundamental at a time. A joint fit of as many fundamentals as sound is better when that number is given (0.619 against 0.601 exact), and worse inside a life, where it is not: held-out onset F1 0.394 against 0.711 at the same 128 bands.

A phrase the life is imitating is taken from what it just heard and not from the declared store. Measured on 169 phrases written as the life writes them, a step read back out of the store names the note that was played in 0.05 of the blocks where the spectrum itself names it in 0.62, at a six-block step and at a one-block step, at 4,000 cells and at 16,000, and with a wider key. The store is what carries a phrase to a later episode, which is the theme.
